claim: SCNR computes the scanner-left world-X XTEMP = BGL − ($8000 − 150*32) = BGL − $6D40; every blip is measured from it.
The blip loop subtracts XTEMP from the object's world X with a 16-bit SUBD, so the projection is modular in the $10000 world cylinder — that modular subtract IS the radar wrap seam.
SCNR reads the object's ABSOLUTE 16-bit world X (OX16) — not an on-screen coordinate — so off-camera attackers still project onto the radar.
The camera-relative position's high byte is shifted right twice (LSRA×2), compressing the 16-bit difference to a 6-bit radar column: (D>>8)>>2 = D>>10.

source.verbatim: SCNR2	LSRA		SHIFT DOWN TO 6 BITS

claim: The scanner strip is 64 columns wide: the terrain-erase loop terminates at (SCANER!>8)+64.
The object's Y is shifted right three times (LSRB×3) to the radar row: y >> 3.
A blip carries the object's colour word OBJCOL — a palette index — stored verbatim into the scanner, never a fresh colour.
